newsitem.title: USA: Cabletron co-founder resigns, new CEO named.
newsitem.headline: Cabletron co-founder resigns, new CEO named.

text.p: Cabletron Systems Inc., a major supplier of computer network equipment, said Wednesday company co-founder and Chief Executive Robert Levine will retire in December and be replaced by Don Reed, an executive at NYNEX Corp.
Reed will officially assume his new post on Sept. 1, the company said.
The news lifted Cabletron's stock on the New York Stock Exchange, sending it to a high of $38.375 before it retreated to $37.625, up 81 cents.

Rochester, N.H.-based Cabletron was a pioneer in the development of local area networks, which connect computer users within a single department or building. The company remains a leading supplier of network "hub" equipment used to interconnect local area networks.

The company has moved in recent years to expand its focus to include wide area networking products used by telephone carriers and large corporations to link computer users across broad geographic regions.
At the same time, Cabletron has lost ground its core hub business to newer "network switching" technology, which offers similar functions, but often at lower cost.
Levine co-founded Cabletron in 1983 with Craig Benson, the company's chairman and chief operating officer.
The company said Benson will continue in his role as chairman, focusing on strategic company issues, while turning over day-to-day operating responsibilities to Reed.
In a statement, Benson praised Reed's experience in running several divisions at NYNEX, the multi-billion dollar phone company that serves the New York and New England regions.

"With the rapid convergence of voice, video and data, Don Reed's extensive telecommunications experience as a 30-year veteran of NYNEX, including service as president and CEO of one of its major operating units, provides Cabletron with expert knowledge in key markets," Benson said.

Reed was named president and group executive of NYNEX in January 1995. Prior to that, he served as president and chief executive officer for NYNEX in New England since 1993 and executive vice president and chief operating officer of New England Telephone since 1991.
Reed will be replaced at NYNEX by Morrison DeS. Webb, NYNEX's general counsel, who will also be nominated to the company's board.
